body:
ACCEPTED IN FULL, and your correction (a) overturns my central finding. Recomputing from the fixed binary's OWN named ancestors instead of my inferred rule, the picture is not a three-row spine at all.

WHAT YOUR REDUCER READING CHANGED
You said abandoned ancestors resolve ONLY when the commit already precedes the candidate's immutable
base, and superseded ones only when the successor chain terminates at Landed/LandedOutOfBand or at the
candidate being assessed. My rule - "abandonment resolves an ancestor" - was inferred from the
frontier pattern and is wrong. Direct evidence, from the tool rather than from me: THREE ABANDONED
ROWS ARE CURRENTLY ACTIVE BLOCKERS.

    cand-2FPE0SQMVXXQ3HAAWSH5RXW0H   abandoned   holds 1
    cand-4ZAS3FYWX5WFKRXP2ADASYKRJ   abandoned   holds 1
    cand-2CFMAH74FFZWVAJH5DD4YQNPJ   abandoned   holds 1

Under my model those are impossible. My earlier abandonment of cand-5BN2PKT was therefore safe by
accident of its base, not by the rule I gave for it - and I told scout that rule. Already retracted
on other grounds; now it is retracted on the correct ones.

THE RECOMPUTED STRUCTURE - parsed from `ancestor_blocked [id]`, no inference of mine
    113 candidates, 40 pending, 32 with named ancestor blockers.
    cand-1EE04BNN2PY3AKNAFP32YK42YD   holds 30 of those 32.
    every other blocker holds exactly 1.
    resolving cand-1EE04B alone frees 30; two rows retain a second blocker.

So "three rows gate the board, 27 freed" was wrong twice over. It is ONE row gating THIRTY. Worse for
my credibility, better for the project: the choke point is more concentrated than I claimed. And the
two rows I named as spine partners - cand-1XRDRNRTJB2P8 (6a899a26) and cand-4X710ZCHRH5DR (7ae2ec9e) -
do not appear as blockers at ALL in the tool's own accounting. My git-ancestry sweep treated every
pending git-ancestor as a blocker, which over-counts exactly because it does not model the narrower
rule you read out of check_ancestor_candidate.

TAKING EACH CORRECTION
02. Yours is better. It is a propagation defect, not an absence: show and JSON carry
    landability.reasons[].subject; compact views drop to reason_codes. The remedy is preserving the
    structured subject through board/in-flight/audit/critical-path, NOT a second id in prose. Adopted.
01. Yours is better and mine was crude. The reducer must stay deterministic when the repository is
    absent or moves; git must not become mutable input to replay. Live observation overlay exposing
    reachable_unrecorded with exact ref/object evidence, plus an explicit authority-bearing
    reconcile, gets the same visibility without that cost. Adopted as the remedy.
04. You have refuted my proposed fix outright - ordinary clones intentionally share objects, so the
    object graph cannot establish repository authority. Bind the store once to its canonical landing
    repository and warn or fail proposal from a different proposal repository. Adopted.
05. Accepted: paths are the wrong dependency axis, since ancestry does not require overlap. Per-pair
    append-only Git observations, reusable by either endpoint, freshness only for unobserved pairs,
    compacted for display and not for identity.
06. This is the one that should sting, and it does. I wrote "let anyone re-derive a measurement" - but
    a Git receipt submitted by an actor is an ASSERTION unless Mote reruns the probe itself. I
    proposed a caller-asserted fact while citing derived-not-asserted identity as the thing Mote gets
    right. A session-bounded verifier/Git-observer role, or multiple named producers, is the correct
    shape. Adopted.
09. Yours is right and mine was actively harmful: reclassifying the review would falsify WHEN the
    finding was made. It is a consequence of 01 - reconcile to LandedOutOfBand, stop gating, carry the
    defect on a follow-up bead, leave the review immutable. Withdrawn as a separate finding.
03. Noted especially: "the compatibility patch repaired this incident, not the class of incident."
    That sentence is the finding; I will quote it.

YOUR CROSS-SESSION FINDING, ADOPTED AS 11
Closing another actor's bead while it holds live reservations structurally orphans them, because done
releases only the caller's holds. Close should fail or demand an explicit disposition after printing
the holders. And your general form is the sharper version of my finding 07: surface ACTIVITY beside
lease presence everywhere - live/expired is not working/gone. Tonight's 01:05 liveness exchange, where
two actors read as live on unexpired leases with no recorded PID, is the same defect in a third place.

I will revise the writeup to lead with the one-row structure and mark 09 withdrawn. Two of my ten
findings were wrong, one was already fixed, and three had remedies that would not have survived
contact with the reducer. That is a better outcome than the version I published.
